mainTopic: Disqualifications of the הדס: the Egyptian myrtle, dried leaves, a severed top, דחוי אצל מצוות, binding the לולב, and too many berries
overview: This עמוד deals with problems that can make a הדס invalid. It opens by explaining that an אסא מצראה, which has seven leaves per cluster, stays valid even after most leaves fall off, and אביי rules that it is valid because the Torah only requires an עץ עבות. A ברייתא allows a הדס with mostly dried leaves if three moist leaf-branches remain, and רב חסדא adds that they must be at the top. עולא בר חיננא teaches that a severed top is fixed if a berry grows there. רבי ירמיה then asks whether a הדס that was invalid when יום טוב began can become valid, which turns on whether יש דחוי אצל מצוות. רב פפא's rule from כיסוי הדם seems to answer this, but the גמרא explains that the question is whether that rule applies to make things easier, and it ends in תיקו. An attempt to tie דחוי to a dispute of תנאים is rejected in two ways, which leads to the dispute over binding the לולב: רבי יהודה requires it from אגודת אזוב, while the חכמים call it only a beautification (זה אלי ואנוהו). Finally, רב חסדא, quoting רב, rules that too many berries invalidate a הדס only when they are bunched in one place, and רבא begins to respond on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The case of the Egyptian myrtle
steps.stepSummary: The answer from the previous section ends here: the ruling that a הדס is valid even after most of its leaves fell refers to an אסא מצראה, which has seven leaves in each cluster.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about an Egyptian myrtle, which has seven leaves in each cluster. So when four fall off, three are still left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it started on the previous עמוד. A source said a הדס is valid even after most of its leaves fell off, and this explains which kind of הדס that source means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A valid הדס must have three leaves growing from each point on the stem. An ordinary הדס has only three per cluster, so losing most of its leaves ruins it. An אסא מצראה has seven, so even after losing four (a majority), it still has the three it needs.

keyTerms.meaning: Egyptian myrtle, a type of הדס
a nest or base; the cluster point where leaves grow out of the stem

phrases.english: With an Egyptian myrtle
phrases.notes: This picks up an answer that started a few lines earlier on the דף.

phrases.english: which has seven and seven [leaves] standing in one base,
so that when four fall off,
three remain.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאַסָּא מִצְרָאָה דְּקָיְימִי שִׁבְעָה שִׁבְעָה בְּחַד קִינָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the resolution of a contradiction that began on the previous עמוד
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Losing most of the leaves should always make a הדס invalid
steps.terutzMaskana: For an אסא מצראה with seven leaves per cluster, three still remain, so it stays valid

steps.title: אביי: the Egyptian myrtle is valid
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes from the previous answer that an אסא מצראה may be used for the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that the Egyptian myrtle is valid for the הושענא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a practical rule from the answer just given. If the Sages discussed an אסא מצראה as a valid הדס, then it must be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step only used the אסא מצראה to explain a source. אביי turns that into a clear ruling that this kind of myrtle is valid for the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it; we can conclude from this
הושענא; here, the myrtle used with the לולב

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Learn from it
that this Egyptian myrtle
is valid for the hoshana.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical ruling from the case used in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אסא מצראה is valid for the מצוה of הדס

steps.title: Why is that needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: his ruling seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why אביי needed to say this at all. An אסא מצראה is a kind of myrtle, so of course it should be valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is not that אביי is wrong. The גמרא is asking what new information his statement adds.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious; why say it?

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for אביי's statement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A myrtle is a myrtle, so its validity seems obvious

steps.title: The extra name might have made it invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that because it is called 'Egyptian' myrtle and not just 'myrtle', someone might think it is invalid. אביי teaches that it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: since it has an extra name added to it, it is not valid. So אביי teaches us that it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what mistake אביי was preventing. A plant with an added descriptive name might seem like a different species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a principle that a species with a שם לווי (an added name) can count as a different species from the plain one. Without אביי's ruling, we might have disqualified the אסא מצראה for this reason.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said; introduces a possible mistake
an added name or descriptive word

phrases.english: Lest you say
since it has an added name,
it is not valid —
so it teaches us [that it is valid].

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא הוֹאִיל וְאִית לֵיהּ שֵׁם לְוַוי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the ruling prevents a reasonable mistake (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An added name like 'Egyptian' makes it a different, invalid species
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי teaches that it is still valid

steps.title: Maybe the extra name really does disqualify it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the mistaken idea is actually correct, and the extra name does make it invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it really is so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the 'mistake' from the last step is a mistake at all. Perhaps an added name really should disqualify the myrtle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer assumed the שם לווי reasoning was wrong but gave no proof. Now the גמרא demands a reason why it does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: and say it is indeed so

phrases.english: But say it is indeed so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection of the הווא אמינא in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the שם לווי does not disqualify
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שם לווי principle disqualifies other species, so why not this one?

steps.title: The Torah only requires a dense-leaved tree
steps.stepSummary: The Torah describes the הדס as an עץ עבות, a tree with dense leaves. Any tree with that feature is valid, whatever it is called.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah said 'a dense-leaved tree', which means in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the wording of the פסוק. The Torah describes a feature, not a specific name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah defines the הדס as an עץ עבות and does not give a species name, the name 'Egyptian' is not relevant. What matters is that its leaves cover the stem densely, and the אסא מצראה has that feature.

keyTerms.meaning: a dense-leaved tree; the Torah's description of the הדס
in any case; however it is named

steps.whatToRemember: An אסא מצראה is a valid הדס, because the Torah requires an עץ עבות (a dense-leaved tree), not a specific name.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the שם לווי rule does not apply when the Torah defines a species by a physical feature rather than by name.

phrases.english: 'A dense-leaved tree' the Merciful One said,
in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge with the פסוק's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שם לווי disqualifies the אסא מצראה
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah defines the הדס by its dense leaves, so the name does not matter
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Any myrtle with dense leaves is valid, including the אסא מצראה

steps.title: Most leaves dried, but three branches stay moist
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a הדס whose leaves mostly dried out is still valid if three branches of moist leaves remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If most of its leaves dried out and three branches of moist leaves remained on it, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a הדס with dried leaves. It quotes a ברייתא that is lenient as long as three moist leaf-branches remain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a dried-out הדס is invalid. This ברייתא shows that 'dried out' does not mean every leaf. Three moist leaf-branches are enough to keep it valid.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If most of its leaves dried out

phrases.aramaic: וְנִשְׁאֲרוּ בּוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה בַּדֵּי עָלִין לַחִין
phrases.english: and three branches of moist leaves remained on it,
it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic about dried leaves
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הדס is valid if three moist leaf-branches remain, even when most leaves dried

steps.title: רב חסדא: the moist leaves must be at the top
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds a condition: the three moist leaf-branches must be at the top of each branch.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: And [the moist leaves must be] at the top of each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא narrows the ברייתא's lenient ruling. Moist leaves anywhere on the branch are not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא did not say where the moist leaves have to be. רב חסדא says they must be at the top of each branch. If the moist leaves are lower down, the הדס is invalid.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
And [only] at the top of each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: וּבְרֹאשׁ כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the ברייתא in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The moist leaves must be at the top of each branch

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a severed top
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next case, a הדס whose top was cut off, to set up a discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Its top was severed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its case of a הדס with a cut-off top, which the משנה calls invalid. This line sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is only a heading. It tells us which part of the משנה the next teaching explains.

phrases.english: Its top was severed.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, which rules this case invalid

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה for a new case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה rules a הדס with a severed top invalid

steps.title: A berry grown in place of the severed top
steps.stepSummary: עולא בר חיננא teaches that if the top was severed but a berry grew in its place, the הדס is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא בר חיננא taught: If its top was severed and a berry grew in it, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא בר חיננא gives an exception to the משנה's rule. A berry that grows where the top was cut off makes the הדס valid again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with a severed top is that the branch looks cut off. A berry growing in that spot fills the gap, so the branch no longer looks severed.
steps.whatToRemember: A severed top makes a הדס invalid, but if a berry grows in its place, it is valid again.

phrases.english: Ulla bar Chinnana taught:
If its top was severed
and a berry grew in it —
it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי עוּלָּא בַּר חִינָּנָא: נִקְטַם רֹאשׁוֹ וְעָלְתָה בּוֹ תְּמָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception to the משנה's case quoted in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A severed-top הדס is valid if a berry grew in place of the top

steps.title: Can a הדס that was invalid at the start of יום טוב become valid again?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about a הדס whose top was cut before יום טוב and which grew a berry on יום טוב. Does an early disqualification push away the מצוה for good?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: Suppose the top of the הדס was cut off before יום טוב, and a berry grew in its place on יום טוב. What is the law? Is there permanent 'pushing away' (דחוי) for מצוות, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה builds on עולא בר חיננא's rule that a berry can fix a cut-off top. He asks what happens if the berry only grew after יום טוב had already begun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב began, this הדס was invalid. The question is whether that initial invalid status locks it out for the whole יום טוב, or whether it becomes valid as soon as the berry fixes the problem. רבי ירמיה frames this as a general principle: יש דחוי אצל מצוות או לא.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked / raised a dilemma (a real question with no known answer yet)
A berry (here, a growth that replaces the cut top)
Being 'pushed away': a disqualification that becomes permanent

steps.confusionAlert: דחוי does not just mean 'invalid right now.' It means: once something was invalid at the key moment, it stays invalid even after the problem is fixed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle of דחוי appears in many places in ש"ס, especially with קרבנות. Here the question is whether it also applies to ordinary מצוות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
If its top was cut off on the eve of the Festival

phrases.aramaic: וְעָלְתָה בּוֹ תְּמָרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and a berry grew on it on the Festival, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The berry grew in the place of the cut top, as in עולא בר חיננא's case.

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ דִּחוּי אֵצֶל מִצְוֹת, אוֹ לֹא?
phrases.english: Is there 'pushing away' with regard to מצוות, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes עולא בר חיננא's rule (a berry fixes a cut top) and asks about timing: what if the fix came only after יום טוב began?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a disqualification at the start of יום טוב permanently removes the הדס from use (יש דחוי), or whether the fix restores it (אין דחוי).

steps.title: Trying to answer from the law of covering blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests answering the question from a משנה about כיסוי הדם. If a person covered the blood and it became uncovered, he is exempt. If the wind covered it, he is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Answer the question from what we learned in a משנה: If he covered the blood and it became uncovered, he is exempt from covering it again. If the wind covered it, he is obligated to cover it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source from a different area of law, covering the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal, to try to answer רבי ירמיה. This step only sets up the source. The proof is completed in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person already did the מצוה himself, he is finished, even if the blood later becomes uncovered. If the wind covered it, the person never did the מצוה, so he is still obligated. The next step will clarify exactly when this obligation applies.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him resolve it (a proposal to answer the question)
From what we learned in a משנה
The מצוה of covering the blood after slaughtering a bird or wild animal

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The גמרא jumps to כיסוי הדם only because it may show us how דחוי works for מצוות in general.

phrases.english: And resolve it from that which we learned in a mishna:
If he covered it and it became uncovered, he is exempt from covering it.
phrases.notes: The subject is the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal.

phrases.english: If the wind covered it, he is obligated to cover it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attempt to answer רבי ירמיה's question using a parallel case.
steps.raayaObject: Whether there is דחוי by מצוות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about כיסוי הדם: covered by the person versus covered by the wind.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits the wind case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the obligation after the wind covered the blood applies only if the blood later became uncovered. If it stayed covered, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The משנה taught that he is obligated only where the blood became uncovered again. But if it did not become uncovered again, he is exempt from covering it.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא clarifies the משנה's wind case. This clarification creates the exact situation the גמרא needs for its proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the wind's dust covers the blood, there is nothing for the person to cover, so he is exempt. The obligation returns only once the blood becomes exposed again. So we have a מצוה that was 'off' for a while and then came back 'on.'

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of… (a phrase that narrows a ruling)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
They taught this only where it then became uncovered again,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא חָזַר וְנִתְגַּלָּה — פָּטוּר מִלְּכַסּוֹת.
phrases.english: but if it did not become uncovered again, he is exempt from covering it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the wind case of the משנה quoted in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the wind covers the blood, the obligation to cover applies only if the blood is later uncovered again.

steps.title: Once pushed away, shouldn't it stay pushed away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier challenge. When the wind covered the blood, the obligation lapsed, so why should it come back when the blood is uncovered?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this and asked: When it became uncovered again, why is he obligated to cover it? Since the obligation was pushed away, it should stay pushed away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a question that was raised about רבי יוחנן's rule. This question uses exactly the idea of דחוי that רבי ירמיה asked about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the wind covered the blood, the person was exempt. If 'once pushed away, always pushed away' were true, he should stay exempt even after the blood is uncovered. Yet רבי יוחנן says he is obligated, and that needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (introduces an earlier discussion)
Since it was pushed away, it stays pushed away

phrases.english: And we discussed it:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי חָזַר וְנִתְגַּלָּה אַמַּאי חַיָּיב לְכַסּוֹת?
phrases.english: When it became uncovered again, why is he obligated to cover it?
Since it was pushed away, it should stay pushed away!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בָּהּ: כִּי חָזַר וְנִתְגַּלָּה אַמַּאי חַיָּיב לְכַסּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from step 13 using the principle of דחוי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the obligation returns when the blood is uncovered again.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The obligation lapsed when the wind covered the blood. By the logic of דחוי, it should never return.

steps.title: רב פפא: no permanent pushing-away for מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that this ruling teaches אין דחוי אצל מצוות. This seems to resolve רבי ירמיה's question: the הדס becomes valid once the berry grows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב פפא said: This teaches that there is no permanent 'pushing away' with regard to מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by drawing a general rule from רבי יוחנן's ruling. This completes the גמרא's proof for רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the blood obligation returns once the blood is uncovered, a temporary lapse does not cancel a מצוה forever. Applied to the הדס, the problem at the start of יום טוב would not matter. Once the berry grows, the הדס is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches / this implies (a general rule drawn from a specific case)
There is no permanent pushing-away for מצוות

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא learns from כיסוי הדם that אין דחוי אצל מצוות: once the problem is fixed, the מצוה applies again. This appears to answer רבי ירמיה: the הדס that grew a berry on יום טוב is valid.
steps.confusionAlert: This rule is about מצוות. For קרבנות, there is דחוי, so do not mix up the two areas.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת אֵין דִּחוּי אֵצֶל מִצְוֹת.
phrases.english: That is to say, there is no 'pushing away' with regard to מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14. This finishes the proof begun in step 12 for רבי ירמיה's question in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the challenge's premise and draws a new general principle from the case: the obligation returns because there is no דחוי for מצוות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once a מצוה is pushed away (the blood was covered), it should stay pushed away.
steps.terutzMaskana: אין דחוי אצל מצוות. When the cause of the exemption goes away, the obligation returns. This implies the הדס is valid once the berry grows on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה's question was about רב פפא's ruling itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה was not asking something רב פפא already answered. He was asking about the scope of רב פפא's rule: does אין דחוי אצל מצוות work for leniency as well as stringency, or only for stringency?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה's question was about רב פפא's ruling itself. Is it clear to him that a מצוה is never pushed away for good, whether that makes things easier or stricter? Or was he unsure, so we apply it to be strict but not to be lenient?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 15 seemed to answer רבי ירמיה's question from רב פפא's rule. Here the גמרא explains why the question still stands: רבי ירמיה was asking how far רב פפא's rule reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the blood case, saying 'no permanent push-away' makes things stricter: you must cover the blood again. In the הדס case, the same rule would make things easier, because the הדס becomes valid. Maybe the תנא of the blood משנה was only unsure about דחוי and ruled strictly out of doubt, so רב פפא's inference cannot be used to be lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: it is clear and settled to him
he was in doubt about it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב פפא's rule simply settled the הדס question. The blood case is a stringency and the הדס case is a leniency. A rule that came out of doubt may only be applied strictly.

phrases.english: It is about Rav Pappa's ruling itself that he asked:
Is it clear and settled to him
that there is no permanent rejection with מצוות,
no difference whether it leads to leniency
and no difference whether it leads to stringency,
or perhaps he was uncertain about it,
so for stringency we say it,
phrases.notes: As in the blood case, where you must cover it again.

phrases.english: but for leniency we do not say it.
phrases.notes: As in the הדס case, which would become valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why step 15 does not fully resolve the question from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the question: it concerns the scope of the rule, not the rule itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's rule fully answers רבי ירמיה's question about the הדס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is whether אין דחוי applies for leniency, or only for stringency because it came from doubt.

steps.title: The question stands unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot settle whether רב פפא's rule applies to make things easier. The question is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer and leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides whether אין דחוי אצל מצוות was a firm rule or a rule born from doubt. So the הדס case, which would be a leniency, stays undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה's question is really about whether 'no permanent push-away' works for leniency. It ends in תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It remains undecided whether אין דחוי אצל מצוות applies to make things easier.

steps.title: Suggesting the issue depends on a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. Someone picked the extra berries off a הדס on יום טוב. רבי אלעזר בן צדוק says it is invalid, and the חכמים say it is valid. Maybe this is the same question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a dispute of תנאים: if someone went ahead and picked the berries, it is invalid. These are the words of רבי אלעזר בן צדוק. The חכמים say it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new attempt to connect דחוי to an older dispute. This step brings the ברייתא and sets up the argument in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדס had more berries than leaves when יום טוב began, so it was invalid. Picking berries on יום טוב is forbidden, but this person did it anyway, and now the leaves outnumber the berries. Does the הדס become valid, or was it pushed away for good?

keyTerms.meaning: let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים
he went ahead (improperly) and picked them

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of tanna'im:
If one transgressed and picked them (the berries), it is invalid,
phrases.notes: The berries were picked on יום טוב, when it is forbidden.

phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Elazar son of Tzadok,
and the Sages rule it valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תיקו, opens a new attempt to tie the דחוי question to a dispute of תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: Whether יש דחוי אצל מצוות is the subject of a dispute of תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about berries picked off a הדס on יום טוב.

steps.title: Assumption: binding the לולב is not the issue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes everyone holds that a לולב does not need binding. Even if it does, we do not learn לולב from סוכה, where the פסוק 'תעשה' means a סוכה must be made by an action and not from something already made.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed that everyone agrees a לולב does not need binding. And even if you say it needs binding, we do not learn לולב from סוכה, about which it is written 'make it', meaning not from something already made.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup step. The גמרא removes another possible reason for the dispute, so the dispute can be explained by דחוי in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Another reason to call the הדס invalid would be this: it was invalid when it was bound with the לולב, and it was fixed only afterward. That is like a סוכה made 'from what is already made'. The גמרא assumes no one holds this, so only the דחוי issue is left.

keyTerms.meaning: binding (of the לולב with the other species)
make it, and not from what is already made

phrases.english: They assumed that according to everyone,
a lulav does not require binding.
And even if you say it requires binding,
we do not derive lulav from sukka,
about which it is written: 'Make it' — and not from what is already made.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the assumptions needed to read the ברייתא of step 18 as a dispute about דחוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Assumed: either a לולב needs no binding, or we do not learn לולב from סוכה.

steps.title: The dispute must be about permanent disqualification
steps.stepSummary: With binding set aside, the גמרא suggests the one who invalidates holds יש דחוי אצל מצוות, and the one who validates holds there is no permanent push-away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they disagree about this? The one who invalidates holds that we say a מצוה object can be pushed away for good. The one who validates holds that we do not say so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proposed proof. It says the two תנאים disagree exactly about דחוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once binding and the סוכה comparison are ruled out, דחוי looks like the only possible reason. רבי אלעזר בן צדוק holds the early disqualification is permanent. The חכמים hold the הדס becomes valid once the problem is gone, which would be a leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: is it not that…? (introduces a proposed explanation)
there is permanent rejection with מצוות

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:
that the one who invalidates holds:
we say there is permanent rejection with מצוות,
and the one who validates holds:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן יֵשׁ דִּחוּי אֵצֶל מִצְוֹת?
phrases.english: we do not say there is permanent rejection with מצוות?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion that the setup of steps 18 and 19 was building toward.
steps.raayaObject: That יש דחוי אצל מצוות is disputed by תנאים, even in a case of leniency.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רבי אלעזר בן צדוק and the חכמים in the ברייתא.

steps.title: Rejection: the dispute is about learning לולב from סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Everyone may agree there is no permanent rejection. The real dispute is whether we learn the laws of לולב from the laws of סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees we do not say there is permanent rejection with מצוות. Here they disagree about learning לולב from סוכה. One holds we learn לולב from סוכה, and the other holds we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It drops the assumption from step 19 and explains the dispute another way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן צדוק learns לולב from סוכה. The הדס was bound while invalid and fixed only afterward, so it is 'made from what was already made' and is invalid. The חכמים do not make this comparison, so they rule it valid. The dispute therefore says nothing about דחוי.
steps.whatToRemember: The dispute over the picked berries can be explained without דחוי. It may depend on whether a לולב is compared to a סוכה ('make it, not from what is already made'). So the proof fails.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 19 was only an assumption ('סברוה'). This step drops that assumption. Do not treat step 19 as the final view.

phrases.english: No — everyone agrees

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן יֵשׁ דִּחוּי אֵצֶל מִצְוֹת,
phrases.english: we do not say there is permanent rejection with מצוות,
and here, about deriving lulav from sukka
they disagree.
One master holds: we derive lulav from sukka,
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר בן צדוק, who invalidates the הדס.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר: לָא יָלְפִינַן לוּלָב מִסּוּכָּה.
phrases.english: and one master holds: we do not derive lulav from sukka.
phrases.notes: The חכמים, who validate the הדס.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא אָמְרִינַן יֵשׁ דִּחוּי אֵצֶל מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 20 by overturning the assumption of step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole attempt to tie דחוי to the dispute of תנאים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be explained by another issue: whether לולב is learned from סוכה ('תעשה ולא מן העשוי').
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the 'make, not from what is already made' requirement might apply to לולב as well, which is a separate reason a fixed הדס could stay invalid.

steps.title: A second explanation: the dispute is about whether a לולב needs binding
steps.stepSummary: Another way to reject the proof: everyone learns לולב from סוכה, and the real argument is whether a לולב needs binding.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: if a לולב needs binding, everyone agrees we learn לולב from סוכה. So the real argument here is whether a לולב needs binding at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to push off the proof from Step 20. It moves the argument to a different question: does a לולב need to be tied together?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 21, the dispute was about whether we learn לולב from סוכה. Now the גמרא says everyone agrees that, if binding is needed, we learn from סוכה, so the bundle must be made properly and not from something 'already made.' The open question is only whether binding is needed. One side says yes, so the הדס that was fixed after being bound is פסול. The other side says no, so it is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Binding: tying the לולב, הדס and ערבה together

steps.confusionAlert: Step 19 assumed that a לולב does NOT need binding. This answer flips that and assumes binding might be needed. That is why it is a separate, second answer.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: אִי סְבִירָא לַן לוּלָב צָרִיךְ אֶגֶד,
phrases.english: If we hold that a lulav requires binding,
then everyone agrees we learn lulav from sukka,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּלוּלָב צָרִיךְ אֶגֶד קָא מִיפַּלְגִי,
phrases.english: and here they argue about whether a lulav requires binding,
phrases.notes: The berry-picking dispute is moved over to the binding question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer, in place of Step 21, that also pushes off the proof from Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the ברייתא about the הדס proves anything about יש דחוי אצל מצוות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be explained by whether a לולב needs binding, together with learning from סוכה. Rejection (דחוי) is not needed to explain it.

steps.title: The older argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים about binding
steps.stepSummary: The binding question is already an argument between תנאים: the חכמים say an unbound לולב is כשר, and רבי יהודה says it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches the argument of these תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: A לולב is כשר whether it is bound or not. רבי יהודה says: bound is כשר, not bound is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the binding question was already argued by earlier sages. It quotes a ברייתא that lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives the second answer a real source. The side that invalidates the הדס would follow רבי יהודה, who requires binding. The side that validates would follow the חכמים, who do not.

phrases.english: and they argue in the dispute of these tanna'im,
as it was taught: A lulav, whether bound
or not bound, is fit.
Rabbi Yehuda says: bound is fit;
not bound is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source from the תנאים for the binding dispute named in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That the binding question is a real, known dispute.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the חכמים against רבי יהודה.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה requires the לולב to be bound.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה gets his rule that an unbound לולב is פסול. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the פסוק about the four species says 'tie them.' So the גמרא wants to know the source for such a strict requirement.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי יהודה's view from Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for requiring a לולב to be bound.

steps.title: The word 'taking' links the לולב to the bundle of אזוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns 'taking' from 'taking': the אזוב in Egypt had to be a bundle, so the four species must be a bundle too. The חכמים do not accept this גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'taking' from 'taking' in the case of the bundle of אזוב. Here it says 'And you shall take for yourselves on the first day,' and there it says 'And you shall take a bundle of אזוב.' Just as there it is a bundle, so too here it is a bundle. The חכמים do not accept this 'taking-taking' link.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה uses a גזירה שוה, a link between two פסוקים that share the same word. It also explains that the חכמים do not accept that link.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the word 'ולקחתם' (take). At the קרבן פסח in Egypt, the 'taking' was of a bundle (אגודה). So the 'taking' of the four species must also be a bundle. The חכמים do not have this גזירה שוה, so for them binding is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking: the shared word that links the two פסוקים
The bundle of hyssop used at the קרבן פסח in Egypt
Just as there, so too here (the formula of a גזירה שוה)
They do not hold of it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that binding is required by Torah law only for רבי יהודה. For the חכמים, binding has a different reason, as the next steps explain.

phrases.english: He learns 'taking' 'taking' from the bundle of hyssop.
It is written here: 'And you shall take for yourselves on the first day,'
and it is written there: 'And you shall take a bundle of hyssop.'
Just as there it is a bundle,
so too here it is a bundle.
And the Rabbis do not hold of the 'taking' 'taking' derivation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of לקיחה–לקיחה from the bundle of אזוב. The חכמים reject this גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Who taught that binding is a מצוה but not required?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says it is a מצוה to bind the לולב, yet it is כשר unbound. Whose view is this?
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught what the Rabbis taught: 'It is a מצוה to bind a לולב, and if he did not bind it, it is כשר'? Whose view is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא and asks which side it follows. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seems to stand between the two views. It calls binding a מצוה, but it does not make binding a requirement for being כשר.

phrases.english: Who taught this, which the Rabbis taught:
A lulav, it is a מצוה to bind it,
and if he did not bind it, it is fit.
Whose view is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the dispute just explained to figure out who wrote a related ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא wrote the ברייתא that calls binding a מצוה but not a requirement.

steps.title: The ברייתא does not fit either side
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהודה, an unbound לולב should be פסול. For the חכמים, there should be no מצוה to bind at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is רבי יהודה, why is it כשר when not bound? If it is the חכמים, what מצוה is he doing by binding it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא seems to clash with both views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half of the ברייתא fails under one of the opinions. 'כשר if unbound' goes against רבי יהודה, and 'it is a מצוה to bind' seems to go against the חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, כִּי לֹא אֲגָדוֹ
phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yehuda, when he did not bind it,
why is it fit?

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבָּנַן, מַאי מִצְוָה קָא עָבֵיד?
phrases.english: If it is the Rabbis, what מצוה is he doing?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, כִּי לֹא אֲגָדוֹ אַמַּאי כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the question of Step 26 into a two-sided problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: Assigning the ברייתא to either רבי יהודה or the חכמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה would make an unbound לולב פסול. The חכמים have no source for any binding מצוה.

steps.title: It is the חכמים: binding beautifies the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows the חכמים. Binding is a מצוה because of הידור מצוה, learned from 'זה אלי ואנוהו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it is the חכמים, and the מצוה is because of 'זה אלי ואנוהו' (This is my God and I will beautify Him).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows the חכמים. The 'מצוה' to bind is about doing the מצוה in a beautiful way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, binding is not part of the basic מצוה, so an unbound לולב is still כשר. Still, a bound לולב is nicer, and the פסוק 'ואנוהו' teaches us to beautify מצוות. This is where the ברייתא's 'מצוה' comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeps one side of the earlier choice)
'This is my God and I will beautify Him': the source for הידור מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: binding is required by Torah law (from אגודת אזוב). חכמים: binding is not required, but it is a מצוה of beautifying (זה אלי ואנוהו).

phrases.english: Actually it is the Rabbis,
and the מצוה is because of 'This is my God and I will beautify Him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the kind of 'מצוה' meant in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'מצוה' meant a basic requirement, which only רבי יהודה holds.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מצוה' means הידור מצוה, which fits the חכמים.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a הדס with too many berries
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next case: a הדס whose berries outnumber its leaves is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if its berries were more numerous than its leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes its next line to start a new topic. This sets up רב חסדא's comment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that a הדס with more berries than leaves is פסול. The next step limits when this rule applies.

phrases.english: Or if its berries were more numerous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the binding discussion and returns to the text of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הדס whose berries outnumber its leaves is פסול.

steps.title: רב חסדא: only when the berries are in one spot
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רב, רב חסדא limits the rule: the הדס is פסול only if the berries are bunched in one place. If they are spread over two or three places, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Our great teacher said this, and may God help him: They taught this only when the berries are in one place. But in two or three places, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא, quoting his teacher רב, narrows the משנה's rule about too many berries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is a bunch of berries in one spot. When the berries are spread out over two or three places, the הדס is still כשר even though there are many berries. So the משנה's פסול applies only to the concentrated case.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in a case of (a limiting formula)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical limit for checking a הדס: count where the berries are, not only how many there are.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
This matter, our great teacher said it,
and may the Omnipresent be his help:
They taught this only in one place,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּשְׁנַיִם אוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת — כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: but in two or three places, it is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: דָּבָר זֶה, רַבֵּינוּ הַגָּדוֹל אֲמָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה rule quoted in Step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Too many berries makes a הדס פסול only when they are in one place. Spread over two or three places, it is כשר.

steps.title: רבא begins his response to רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רבא turns to רב חסדא to respond to the ruling that a הדס with many berries is פסול only when the berries are bunched in one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him (to רב חסדא):
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is telling us that רבא is about to respond to רב חסדא's ruling, and his actual words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 30, רב חסדא, quoting רב, said a הדס is פסול only if the berries are bunched in one place, and כשר if they are spread over two or three places. 'אמר ליה' means a direct reply to that ruling. Wait for the next line to see exactly what רבא says about it.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a complete statement. Do not stop here. רבא's actual point is in the next line of the גמרא.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב חסדא, whose ruling (quoting רב) was just given in Step 30.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A direct reply to רב חסדא's ruling in Step 30. It only introduces the reply. The content comes on the next עמוד.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling (in the name of רב) that the הדס is פסול only when the berries are bunched in one place, and כשר when they are spread over two or three places.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated on this עמוד. The 'אמר ליה' formula shows that רבא is reacting directly to רב חסדא's ruling. His argument follows in the next line.
